Going Bacharach: The Songs of an Icon, a new revue that clocks in at roughly 100 minutes—including an intermission—manages to intelligently document its subject’s dazzling career and distinctive artistry while keeping the emphasis squarely where it should be, on the music itself.

Going Bacharach: The Songs of an Icon , a musical retrospective of Burt Bacharach and (mostly) Hal David, summons up the mid-century master of pop with verve and style, and reminds us of what a singular, infectious sound he perfected.

This musical revue does include all the Bacharach songs you would want to hear as well as some unfamiliar ones.
Going Bacharach: The Songs of an Icon is the world of music in our lives on the stage at The Marjorie S. Deane Little Theater and it is a must see, must experience.
Going to Going Bacharach means you’re going to have a grand time at a show that’s going for the gold in more ways than one.

This new show, Going Bacharach: The Songs of an Icon at The Marjorie S. Deane Little Theater is a gem, and if you've never fallen in love with a Burt Bacharach tune, this bursting-with-talent revue of his work is bound to make you think twice.

Going Bacharach is a visually and musically enchanting legacy evening that honors a prodigious composer, one who successfully weathered shifting tastes and changing trends in one of the world’s most competitive and sometime brutal industries.
It becomes what it was meant to be: a celebration of Bacharach’s genius, interpreted by three stellar voices and an ensemble that, when finally united, reminds us why this music matters.
For me, Going Bacharach doesn’t sufficiently honor the first nor go far enough in the direction of the second.

cn.t: Critics warmly embrace this Bacharach revue, praising its talented performers and lovingly curated celebration of the iconic composer's sophisticated melodies and enduring songbook.
